key_insight: In ultra-high-resolution photon-counting CT of the lung, deep learning reconstruction reduced noise while preserving lesion contrast and improving measured spatial resolution and texture fidelity versus hybrid iterative reconstruction.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest DLR may help produce sharper, less noisy lung CT images at lower doses, which could support more reliable characterization of small nodules and parenchymal detail.
method: Patient-derived 3D-printed lung phantom with three inserted lesions
UHR photon-counting CT imaging at 4 dose levels (6, 4, 2, and 1 mGy)
Compared hybrid iterative reconstruction vs UHR deep learning reconstruction using noise, contrast, CNR, MTF, histograms, and GLCM
evidence_signal: Across the phantom and illustrative patient cases, DLR lowered noise, maintained contrast, improved MTF50 by about 0.4 lp/mm, and narrowed attenuation distributions while preserving mean attenuation.
watch_item: Results come from a prototype system, a controlled phantom, and only two patient examples, so broader clinical performance and generalizability still need validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning Reconstruction for Ultra-High-Resolution Photon-Counting CT of the Lung: Image Quality and Texture Characterization
